assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reorganised international trade theory and empirics. It explains who exports, why gains from trade are reallocative, and how trade affects aggregate productivity. The framework is now standard in trade, macro and industrial organisation, and it complements the earlier prize for new trade theory without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is Melitz's 2003 model together with the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exports versus FDI. Helpman has a broader foundational role across trade theory. Redding's contributions lie more in quantitative and spatial extensions, so I do not include him in the core credit.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of replication, extension and empirical confirmation. The firm-level stylised facts are robust and the framework is widely taught.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit Redding for quantitative extensions.
Overlap with the Grossman-Helpman and quantitative Ricardian candidates on trade.
Welfare implications depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how empirical researchers state what data can and cannot reveal under weak assumptions. It is a principled complement to design-based causal inference: it asks what is identified before assuming enough to point-identify. Applications span policy analysis, treatment effects and incomplete structural models.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator (bounds, the reflection problem, the logic of credible inference). Tamer is central to moment-inequality methods and incomplete models. Molinari is a leading contributor to inference, but her work is later and more technical, so I leave her out of the core credit.
assessment.maturity: The ideas date from the late 1980s and 1990s and have been developed over decades. Adoption in applied work is real but narrower than that of point-identified designs.
uncertainties: Applied uptake is smaller than the conceptual importance suggests.
Manski has not been recognised earlier, and the committee may weigh breadth of applied impact against methodological depth.
Division of credit between Manski and the moment-inequality literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work built modern political economics: how electoral rules, constitutions and political incentives shape fiscal policy, state capacity and public-goods provision. It links formal theory to cross-country and within-country evidence and has shaped a large research field and policy debate on institutions.
assessment.attribution: Persson-Tabellini (constitutions, electoral rules, fiscal outcomes) and Besley-Persson (state capacity, taxation, conflict) are tightly linked and largely co-authored. The three form a coherent group, though others have contributed in adjacent areas.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of development, with books, replication and a mature empirical literature. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity was awarded for related but distinct questions, so overlap is partial.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2024 institutions prize may lower priority.
Causal identification in the cross-country constitutional evidence is contested.
Credit relative to other political-economy theorists not listed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reshaped understanding of how technology and trade change labour demand, wages and local labour markets. It combines the task framework, the skill-premium literature and credible quasi-experimental evidence on import competition. The policy relevance is large.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Hanson are central, through the China-shock design and task-based analysis. Katz is foundational in the skill premium and the race between education and technology. Dorn is a major co-author of the China-shock work, and the task framework also rests on contributors outside this list, such as Levy and Murnane, which complicates the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of work with extensive replication. The long-run magnitude and persistence of trade effects have been refined and debated.
uncertainties: Task-framework credit is shared with scholars not on the list.
Debates over magnitudes and external validity of the China-shock estimates.
Katz's adjacency to the 2023 prize on women's labour-market outcomes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combining tax records with national accounts to measure long-run top incomes and wealth changed the empirical agenda on inequality and put distribution back at the centre of macro and public economics. It is also highly influential in policy debates.
assessment.attribution: The top-incomes series is mainly Piketty and Saez, with Atkinson (deceased) an important antecedent. Zucman's offshore-wealth work is important but newer and could belong to a separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of data and extensive follow-up. Measurement remains actively disputed, so confirmation is partial.
uncertainties: Disagreement over measurement choices, such as treatment of transfers and tax-unit definitions.
Theoretical claims about r > g are less secure than the measurement contribution.
Credit for Atkinson, who died in 2017, and for Zucman.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins the way central banks model and conduct monetary policy. Its importance for policy and for macro methodology is very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely dispersed among Calvo, Taylor, Christiano-Eichenbaum, Gali-Gertler, Woodford, Smets and others. A three-person limit forces a contested selection. Woodford, Gali and Gertler are proposed as the most synthetic contributors to the modern framework, but the choice is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in policy institutions. The framework has been tested, extended and criticised, and has had to adapt to heterogeneity and the zero lower bound.
uncertainties: Severe credit-allocation problem across at least eight names.
Empirical evidence for some core ingredients, such as the Phillips curve, is mixed.
Macro prizes on rational expectations and DSGE already cover nearby ground.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Duffie's work on credit-risk modelling, the pricing of defaultable securities and the theory of over-the-counter markets shaped how financial markets and intermediaries are analysed and regulated. The Duffie-Garleanu-Pedersen search model is a standard framework for decentralised markets and links to policy on market structure and clearing.
assessment.attribution: Duffie is the central figure across credit risk and OTC markets. Pedersen has important and distinct contributions in the OTC search and liquidity literature. Garleanu is a co-author of the key search paper but a less central figure overall.
assessment.maturity: Credit-risk and OTC-market theory are well established, with two decades of extensions and regulatory use. Empirical testing of the search models is more limited.
uncertainties: Finance has had several recent prizes, so diversity across fields may affect priority.
Pedersen's work overlaps with the separate liquidity candidate.
Direct empirical validation of the search mechanisms is partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combining machine learning with causal inference, via double or debiased machine learning, causal forests and heterogeneous treatment effects, extends the credibility-revolution toolkit to high-dimensional settings. The methods are used widely in applied work and in industry, which gives them substantial impact.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov is a principal author of the debiased machine-learning framework. Athey has made major contributions to the causal-forest and policy-learning literature and to the application of the methods in economics. Wager is a central statistical co-author, but the methodological credit comes mainly from the other two.
assessment.maturity: The literature is roughly a decade old. Adoption is fast, but the long-run influence on empirical practice is not yet settled, and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Relatively recent work, so the time test is limited.
Overlap with the 2021 prize on causal inference, and credit shared with statisticians and computer scientists.
Overlap with other candidates carrying Athey's or Chernozhukov's names.
